items.speaker_state: He is matter-of-factly explaining what the paw can do.
items.scene: At the Whites' home, the retired sergeant-major explains the paw after showing it to them.
evidence: He showed them a small, dry monkey's paw.
The paw gives three wishes

items.speaker_state: He is cautioning them about the consequences of using the paw.
items.scene: At the Whites' home, he warns them about trying to change their fate.
items.reaction_to_previous: He adds a warning to his explanation that the paw grants three wishes.
evidence: The paw gives three wishes,
But trying to change your fate brings sadness.

items.speaker_state: Mr. White is curious about the sergeant-major's experience with the wishes.
items.scene: At the Whites' home, Mr. White asks the sergeant-major whether he used the paw's wishes.
items.reaction_to_previous: He follows the warning by asking whether the sergeant-major made any wishes.
evidence: But trying to change your fate brings sadness.
Did you make any wishes?

items.speaker_state: He matter-of-factly answers Mr. White's question.
items.scene: At the Whites' home, the sergeant-major tells Mr. White that he has used all three wishes.
items.reaction_to_previous: He directly answers Mr. White's question about whether he made any wishes.
evidence: Did you make any wishes?
I've already used all three wishes.

items.speaker_state: He is warning Mr. White not to use the paw and not to hold him responsible for what follows.
items.scene: At the Whites' home, the sergeant-major warns Mr. White after he pulls the paw from the fire.
items.reaction_to_previous: He follows his admission that he used all the wishes with a warning about the paw.
evidence: The soldier suddenly threw the paw into the fire.
Mr. White quickly pulled it out.
Burn it, or don't blame me for what happens,

items.speaker_state: Herbert is joking about the paw and suggests a practical use for a wish.
items.scene: After the guest leaves, Herbert jokes about asking the paw for money to pay for the house.
evidence: After their guest left, Herbert joked,
That would pay for the house.

items.speaker_state: Mr. White makes the wish while smiling and raising the paw.
items.scene: At the Whites' home, Mr. White raises the paw and wishes for two hundred pounds.
items.reaction_to_previous: He acts on Herbert's suggestion to ask the paw for two hundred pounds.
evidence: Mr. White smiled as he raised the paw.
Ask for two hundred pounds, Father! That would pay for the house.

items.speaker_state: He delivers the news in a restrained, matter-of-fact way; no feeling is stated.
items.scene: At the Whites' home, a man from Herbert's company tells them how their son died.
evidence: Later, a man from Herbert's company came to visit.
Your son died after a machine caught him at work,

items.speaker_state: He explains the company's position and its offer in restrained terms.
items.scene: At the Whites' home, the company visitor explains its position and offers money for the loss.
items.reaction_to_previous: He follows the news of Herbert's death with the company's response and offer.
evidence: Your son died after a machine caught him at work,
The company says it isn't to blame, but offers two hundred pounds for your loss.

items.speaker_state: Mrs. White is grieving and urgently wants Herbert brought back to life.
items.scene: A week after the funeral, she urges her husband to use the paw to bring Herbert back.
items.reaction_to_previous: She rejects the company's offer as the focus and urges her husband to use the remaining wishes.
evidence: A week after the funeral, Mrs. White woke her husband with tears on her face.
There are still two wishes in the paw! Bring our son back to life!

items.speaker_state: Mr. White is afraid of what might return and reluctant to make the wish.
items.scene: After Mrs. White urges him to bring Herbert back, Mr. White voices his fear.
items.reaction_to_previous: He responds to her demand by explaining why he fears bringing Herbert back.
evidence: There are still two wishes in the paw! Bring our son back to life!
You didn't see him, and I'm afraid of what might return.

items.speaker_state: Mrs. White insists that Herbert is their son, appealing to her husband's attachment to him.
items.scene: After Mr. White expresses fear about what might return, Mrs. White argues for bringing Herbert back.
items.reaction_to_previous: She counters Mr. White's fear by reminding him that Herbert is their son.
evidence: You didn't see him, and I'm afraid of what might return.
But he's our own son!

items.speaker_state: Mr. White makes the wish while his voice is shaking, suggesting fear or unease.
items.scene: Downstairs in the darkness, Mr. White makes a wish for Herbert to live again as his wife follows him.
items.reaction_to_previous: He gives in after Mrs. White insists that Herbert is their son.
evidence: his voice was shaking.
But he's our own son!
I wish for Herbert to live again.

items.speaker_state: Mrs. White recognizes the person at the door as Herbert and is eager to reach him.
items.scene: In the darkness, after a quiet knock, Mrs. White identifies the person at the door as Herbert.
evidence: A quiet knock broke the silence.
She ran towards the door, pulling free when Mr. White caught her arm.
It's Herbert!

items.speaker_state: Mr. White is urgently trying to stop Mrs. White from opening the door.
items.scene: As heavy knocks shake the door, Mr. White searches the floor for the paw and calls for her to wait.
evidence: The door shook with each heavy knock.
Just as she reached to open the door, he grabbed the paw and made his third and last wish.
Please wait!
